claims.text: Conventionally cast eutectic high-entropy alloys have a straight-lamellar microstructure.
The initial straight-lamellar alloy exhibits balanced mechanical properties.
The initial straight-lamellar alloy has limited work-hardening and interfacial effects.
Directional solidification with controlled cooling rates will naturally kink straight eutectic lamellae into a vermicular morphology.
A subsequent annealing and cold-rolling sequence will stabilize the vermicular microstructure.
A vermicular eutectic morphology introduces a greater area and a broader directional distribution of heterogeneous interphase boundaries.
The additional interphase boundaries impede or pin dislocations.
The additional interphase boundaries act as energy-absorption sites during crack propagation.
Enhanced phase-boundary pinning reduces dislocation pile-up.
Enhanced phase-boundary pinning improves load distribution between phases.
Increased interfacial area and kinked morphology promote additional strain hardening.
The kinked morphology delays crack initiation.
The vermicular microstructure will increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to a straight-lamellar microstructure.
The vermicular microstructure will increase uniform tensile elongation relative to a straight-lamellar microstructure.
The vermicular microstructure will modestly increase Young's modulus or at least maintain high stiffness.
The vermicular microstructure will enhance fracture toughness.
Insufficient control of the thermal gradient can prevent formation of the vermicular structure and eliminate the expected benefits.
The magnitude and reproducibility of the property improvement depend on alloy composition, cooling conditions, and post-solidification treatment.

contradictions.description: Failure to form the vermicular structure is treated in the boundary statement as an excluded processing condition under which benefits are not expected, but the falsification rule treats failure to reproducibly form that structure as decisive falsification of the hypothesis.
